articles.summary: At the heart of Silvretta — aCentauri Solar Racing‘s solar-powered challenger car entry in the grueling 3,022-kilometer Bridgestone World Solar Challenge (BWSC) across the Australian Outback — is a power electronics circuit using PowiGaN gallium nitride (GaN) technology from Power Integrations.
articles.title: PowiGaN Proves Its Value in Extreme Solar Challenge

articles.summary: In 2023, while chasing solar-powered cars across the Australian Outback during the Bridgestone World Solar Challenge (BWSC), I found myself behind the wheel of a petrol-powered van. The irony wasn’t lost on anyone...
articles.title: Driving a Gas-Powered Van in the Middle of a Solar Car Race

articles.summary: Every two years, innovative young minds from around the world gather in Australia for a race unlike any other. The Bridgestone World Solar Challenge isn’t about speed—it’s about pushing the boundaries of what’s possible with solar energy, power electronics, and human ingenuity.
articles.title: Racing the Sun — How the 2025 World Solar Challenge is Pushing the Limits of Efficiency and Reliability

articles.summary: Designing a solar race car requires not only mechanical ingenuity but also highly efficient and compact electronics to manage power delivery across the vehicle. In this post, we explore the challenges of providing a DC-DC power supply for such a demanding application—and how Power Integrations rose to meet them.
articles.title: Challenges of Providing a DC-DC Power Supply for Solar Race Car Applications

articles.summary: In the fast-evolving world of electric vehicles (EVs), battery technology remains the linchpin of innovation. In 2025, the industry is seeing a wave of advancements that are expanding range, slashing charging times, and lowering costs, all while improving sustainability.
articles.title: Electric Vehicle Batteries in 2025: Redefining the Road Ahead

articles.summary: In 1987, a newspaper ad caught the eye of a physics professor in Sydney. It was a call to adventure: build a car powered only by the sun and race it 3,000 kilometers across the Australian Outback. That professor was John Storey— and nearly four decades later, Storey is still at the heart of the Bridgestone World Solar Challenge.
articles.title: John Storey and the Solar Spirit — A Life Devoted to Sustainability and Innovation
